groups.text: It is currently 26 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Republican legislators are pressuring the Trump administration to ban American firms from buying memory chips from ChangXin Memory Technologies, a Chinese manufacturer the Pentagon flagged as military-linked in 2025. This push follows reports that Apple has been lobbying for clearance to source CXMT's DRAM chips since May, sparking a national security debate over whether such revenue fuels China's defense and AI capabilities. While US firms face these restrictions, Thinking Machines Lab, founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, has released Inkling. This multimodal open-weights model leads other US labs on agentic tasks but still trails the best Chinese models in overall performance and factual accuracy. Meanwhile, the rise of AI agents is shifting financial markets. Brokerage infrastructure startup Alpaca has raised 435 million dollars to enter prime brokerage services after its API trading volume surged four times in the first quarter of 2026.

Protesters have taken to the streets in Kyiv and Brussels following President Volodymyr Zelensky’s decision to dismiss Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. As he exits his role, Fedorov has filed paperwork to use EU loans for the purchase of PAC-3 missiles. Ukraine is critically short of these anti-ballistic missiles, which are the only tools capable of downing Russian ballistic missiles targeting civilians in Kyiv. This request contrasts with a recent defense package from European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, which focused on deep strike missiles rather than anti-ballistic technology. In other news, Vice President JD Vance told Joe Rogan that Jeffrey Epstein had connections to the highest levels of American and Israeli intelligence. Meanwhile, students in the machine learning community are reporting frustration over ECCV registration fees. Those presenting papers cannot use the early bird student rate of 440 dollars and must instead pay a full registration fee of 805 dollars.

The United States and Iran have exchanged fire for a sixth day, straining a preliminary deal to end the war. Washington launched a six-hour wave of strikes against Iranian command centers, air defense sites, and coastal surveillance facilities in locations including Greater Tunb Island and Bandar Abbas to degrade threats in the Strait of Hormuz. In response, Tehran struck targets in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan. This escalation follows warnings from President Donald Trump that Iran must return to negotiations or face attacks on its energy infrastructure. Meanwhile, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that soldiers aged 30 and older will now undergo testosterone testing during annual health exams to optimize performance, calling the preservation of the individual fighter a holy duty. In Europe, Russian forces used an FPV drone to attack people near Hryhorivka in the Zaporizhzhia district, injuring two boys aged 15 and 17.

The Trump administration is increasing pressure on Brazil, with the United States set to impose a 25 percent tariff on most imports from the country starting July 22. This move follows a Section 301 investigation into illegal deforestation and Brazilian digital trade practices, which officials say create an uneven playing field for American producers. The levies will cover a wide range of goods, from machinery to sugar, after negotiations between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer collapsed. While these tariffs may strain diplomatic relations and pressure Brazil's currency, they contrast with the push for regulatory stability in the U.S. digital asset market. Ripple’s Chief Legal Officer Stuart Alderoty is currently urging the Senate not to vote against the CLARITY Act, arguing that a lack of framework leaves 67 million American crypto holders exposed to bad actors. Meanwhile, Argentine goalkeeper Emi Martínez, a global brand ambassador for Zoomex, has vowed to retire from the national team if Argentina wins back-to-back World Cups.

Cybersecurity researchers are warning of a surge in rapid and deceptive digital attacks. A new ransomware actor called Spirals recently breached an IT services firm in South Asia, moving from initial access to data theft and network encryption in less than twenty-four hours. Meanwhile, Russian hackers tracked as UAT-11795 are using trojanized installers for common apps like Zoom and WebEx to deploy the Starland remote access trojan. This malware targets users in the U.S., Germany, Romania, and Venezuela to steal cryptocurrency and browser credentials. In a different sector, Amylyx Pharmaceuticals is approaching a pivotal moment this quarter as it prepares to read out results from a study on avexitide. The drug is designed to prevent severe drops in blood sugar for patients who have undergone stomach-reducing surgery for weight loss. This comes two years after the company voluntarily pulled an ALS drug from the market.

In the software world, developers at llama.cpp are fixing a technical inconsistency that broke integrated-GPU host-buffer use on ROCm. The update restores the integrated property for HIP builds to ensure AMD APU and UMA parts function correctly. This change guards a previous workaround used to prevent corrupted output on Jetson Orin, ensuring that fix remains intact for CUDA builds while restoring necessary flags for HIP. Meanwhile, in the industrial sector, Insteel Industries has filed a Form 8-K with the SEC. The North Carolina-based steel manufacturer provided updated financial statements and exhibits regarding its results of operations and overall financial condition. While one update addresses the granular stability of local AI hardware acceleration, the other provides a formal disclosure of corporate health for a public company in the blast furnace and rolling mill industry.

In Iran, the new supreme leader and state-controlled media are calling for retaliation to avenge the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. During a July 14 parliamentary session, more than 180 of 290 lawmakers waved red flags demanding revenge, while the daily Hamshahri published a wanted list of 13 Western politicians and military officials, including German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. This escalation in rhetoric contrasts with other regional crises, such as in Algeria, where drought and heatwaves triggered over 130 fires on July 15, killing at least one person and causing significant damage for farmers. Meanwhile, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is visiting Morocco amid new revelations regarding the Moroccan surveillance apparatus. Forbidden Stories reports that representatives from the Israeli company NSO spent ten days in a Rabat villa in 2017, adding to the long-standing scandal involving Pegasus spyware used against high-ranking French officials.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with rain chances up to 83 percent and temperatures between 23 and 32 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Sommerferien 2026 Berlin, Arbeitslos melden, and Ende Merantix, at 13:00, Open Office - Platform Team at Momentum office couch area, at 14:00, Meeting Aaron, at 16:00, AutoML Seminar, and at 19:00, ️ Greifen and ️ Greifen.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
